vram_note: the 72 GB variant; budgets here are computed against a 48 GB cap (49152 MB) - a sizing policy, not a measurement

datasheet.notes: dense (non-sparse) figures. The product-page headline is FP4-sparse; the dense ladder de-rates it FP4/2 = FP8, FP8/2 = FP16, and INT8 TOPS = FP8 TFLOPS. fp32 = 14080 cores x 2 x 2.377 GHz official boost = 66.9 TFLOPS. Clock ladder: base 1755 / boost 2377 / max-boost 3090 - max-boost is what clocks.max.graphics reports, a best-case bin and not a sustained promise, so do not size against it. Bandwidth 1344 GB/s is stated as 'up to'. Note the vendor's own published peak columns imply a clock ~8-10% above each SKU's stated max, so treat any datasheet-derived peak as an upper bound.

open_items: ECC is configurable and disabled by default; ceilings and byte budgets here were measured in that state. If the deployed part ships ECC-on, re-measure the bandwidth ceiling and re-run the dial before final sizing - bandwidth is the decisive axis

Programmable power (-pl, down to ~150 W; persistent via SMBPBI) enables a power-matched per-watt experiment vs Thor (e.g. -pl 150) - optional, would replace the nameplate-based 2-2.6x per-watt estimate with a measured one
MIG (two instances) is supported - a hardware-isolation option when co-locating a latency-critical model

clock_sources.note: prefer a persistent pynvml handle; nvidia-smi subprocess fallback allowed at reduced rate

sm_lock_note: This part's governor holds POWER, not clock: a 2160 MHz request realizes ~2092 cold and settles 2047-2062 warm at the 300 W cap, wandering lower over a long soak while throughput holds within 10%. Lock the warm-settled bin (2062) rather than a boost bin, so requested==realized for every workload class - a light workload floats above an upper-bound lock with no power-cap flag asserted, which makes drift adjudication hard-fail on an otherwise healthy run. drift_report.py demotes a power-governed SM deviation to WARN only when memory PASSes, the sole reason is the software power cap, and the median deviation is <= 10%.
mem_lock_note: nameplate 14001 MHz does not hold under tensor load on this card - memory pins one supported bin down at 13365; locking there keeps requested==realized so verify_lock judges on honest terms (measured 2026-08-07)

power_sources.note: power.draw via NVML/nvidia-smi - no sysfs rails on discrete

emc_dial.note: memory/SM sensitivity via -lmc/-lgc at 80% of max inside the pipeline (RUN_CLOCK_DIAL=1); no devfreq dial on discrete

ops_per_tinst_note: fp16 calibrated on-box against the known-truth 137.44 GFLOP GEMM (snap error 0.00%). Note it is 4x the sm_110 value - these constants do NOT transfer across architectures. int8/fp8 are uncalibrated: calibrate against a known-truth engine at that precision before running a roofline on those pipes, or it will refuse.
quirks: -lgc/-lmc can silently not take (observed 2026-07: locked file read 180/405 MHz while log claimed 3090/14001) - verify under load, never trust an idle read-back

SM lock realizes at the boost-table tensor-load clock (~2570 observed for a 3090 request), and the realized clock is WORKLOAD-DEPENDENT at the power cap (2437 under a light GEMM, 2167 under a heavy one) - hence the sm_lock_mhz sustained-bin policy; the reference clock is the REALIZED value, never the requested one

torch typed int8 path (_int_mm) failed on sm_120 with pre-cu13x builds (cuBLAS INVALID_VALUE) - run the GEMM canary before trusting torch probes; int8 ceiling falls back to the TRT path if typed probes fail
idle discrete GPUs legitimately downclock even when locked - an idle clock read proves nothing about the lock
sampler_period_note: 73.1 ms: not commensurate with 20/30 Hz row periods. NVML power.draw is a ~1 s hardware average on this card (aliasing does not bite as it did with Thor's instantaneous ina238 register), the period is kept for consistency with the Thor sweep
_README: A filled, working example (RTX PRO 5000 Blackwell, discrete). Values from the public product page plus this card's own lock/drift measurements. Copy the template for other devices. Machine-specific configs you add should be named <name>.local.json (gitignored).
required_power_mode_note: jetson-only (nvpmodel); null on discrete, where the power cap is a -pl setting rather than a mode
